summary: Failure modes generated and agreement-checked from 172 traces.

codes.name: Execution_Timeout
codes.description: An agent or code execution step exceeds the allowed time budget (>600s), causing the run to be forcibly terminated before producing a valid output. Any null or absent output subsequently forwarded to downstream agents is a direct propagation consequence of this event, not a separate root cause.
codes.when_to_use: When a run is terminated due to wall-clock or CPU time limits being exceeded, regardless of which agent or step was running at the time.
codes.when_not_to_use: When execution completes within time limits but produces wrong or partial output due to logic errors. Do not apply when an unhandled exception (not a timeout signal) is the termination cause — use A.4 instead.

codes.name: Runtime_Exception_Or_Silent_Return_Failure
codes.description: Covers two closely related failure modes that both abort or bypass normal output production: (a) the executed code raises an unhandled exception or traceback during runtime, terminating execution before a valid output is produced; (b) the function completes without exception but returns None, an incomplete dict, or a dict missing required keys (e.g., 'circles', 'all_scores') due to a silent logic error — a condition that is structurally indistinguishable from an exception-driven null at the point of downstream consumption. Any null value propagated to downstream agents as a result of either sub-case is a propagation consequence of this code. Formerly split as A.4 (Runtime_Exception) and C.4 (Incomplete_Return_Structure); merged because C.4 was exclusively a symptom of A.4 or A.1, with only the silent-return sub-case representing genuinely distinct behavior.
codes.when_to_use: When execution raises an unhandled exception (traceback visible in logs), OR when the function returns without exception but the return value is None, missing required keys, or structurally incomplete such that downstream validation fails.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the failure is due to a timeout (use A.1). When the output is structurally complete but semantically incorrect or violates domain constraints (use appropriate B or C codes). When the output is null solely because of downstream propagation of an upstream agent's failure — tag the upstream event as A.1 or A.4 and the propagation hop as A.3.

codes.name: Null_Output_Propagation
codes.description: A secondary/propagation-layer code. An agent receives None, an empty value, or an absent output as its input — originating from an upstream timeout (A.1) or runtime/return failure (A.4) — and forwards this null value further downstream without halting the pipeline or raising an explicit error. This code is NOT a root cause; it documents that a null failure crossed at least one agent handoff boundary and that the pipeline lacked a null-guard at that handoff point. Must always be co-tagged with the upstream root cause code (A.1 or A.4).
codes.when_to_use: When a null or absent value produced by an upstream failure (A.1 or A.4) is confirmed to have been passed across a handoff boundary to a downstream agent, and that downstream agent attempted to process it. Apply in addition to, never instead of, the originating root-cause code.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the null value was caught and handled gracefully (pipeline halted cleanly, error surfaced correctly). When there is no confirmed handoff crossing — i.e., the null remained within the originating agent's scope. Do not use as a standalone root-cause code.

codes.name: Context_Overflow_Or_Memory_Loss
codes.description: An agent loses access to critical prior information due to context window exhaustion, context truncation by the runtime, or failure to retain or retrieve relevant state across turns or handoffs. This manifests as the agent acting as if earlier instructions, problem constraints, intermediate results, or prior conversation turns do not exist, producing outputs that are inconsistent with or ignorant of established context.
codes.when_to_use: When an agent's output is inconsistent with information that was demonstrably provided earlier in the conversation or trajectory, and the most parsimonious explanation is that the earlier content fell outside the active context window or was not retrieved. Also applies when token-count logs confirm truncation occurred.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the agent has access to the context but chooses to ignore or contradict it (use A.7 for instruction non-compliance). When the inconsistency is due to a logic or reasoning error rather than missing context. When the context was never provided in the first place.

codes.name: Behavioral_Anomaly
codes.description: An agent exhibits pathological behavioral patterns that prevent forward progress without producing a conventional exception or timeout. Includes: (a) looping — repeatedly generating the same or near-identical output across successive steps without convergence; (b) perseveration/repetition — re-executing already-completed sub-tasks or re-raising already-resolved issues; (c) refusal — declining to attempt the assigned task citing inability, policy, or ambiguity when the task is within scope; (d) capability degradation — producing outputs of markedly lower quality or coherence than earlier steps in the same run without an identifiable external cause.
codes.when_to_use: When an agent produces multiple substantially identical outputs in succession (looping/repetition), explicitly refuses a valid in-scope task (refusal), or shows a step-change drop in output quality or coherence within a single run that cannot be attributed to bad input, timeout, or exception.
codes.when_not_to_use: When repeated output is the correct behavior (e.g., legitimately re-checking a constraint). When refusal is appropriate (out-of-scope or unsafe request). When quality drop is explained by bad upstream input — tag the upstream cause instead. When the agent is simply slow but making progress — use A.1 if it times out.

codes.name: Instruction_Non_Compliance
codes.description: An agent receives a well-formed, in-scope instruction but fails to comply with it in one or more of the following ways: (a) ignoring or overriding the system prompt's constraints or role definition; (b) solving a different problem than the one specified (task substitution); (c) producing output in the wrong format, schema, or structure when the correct format was explicitly specified and the agent had context to follow it. This code covers deliberate or negligent deviation from stated instructions, distinguishable from capability failure (the agent could comply but did not).
codes.when_to_use: When the instruction was clear and in-scope, the agent demonstrably had access to it (no context loss), and the output does not conform to what was asked — whether in terms of task identity, output format, or behavioral constraints defined in the system prompt.
codes.when_not_to_use: When non-compliance is caused by context loss or truncation (use A.5). When the format violation results from an exception or null return (use A.4). When the agent attempted to comply but made a reasoning or domain error — that is a correctness failure, not a compliance failure. When the instruction itself was malformed or contradictory.

codes.name: Solver_Degenerate_Initial_Configuration
codes.description: Solver generates an initial circle placement configuration where circles are clustered, stacked on boundaries, or placed at minimal radii (e.g., r≈0), resulting in a degenerate starting point that undermines any subsequent optimization. This is a named sub-pattern of incorrect constraint enforcement during initialization.
codes.when_to_use: When the solver's initial placement (before any optimization pass) produces circles that are visibly degenerate — near-zero radii, identical positions, all circles pushed to boundary edges, or collapsed into a cluster — indicating initialization constraints were not properly enforced.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not apply if the degenerate appearance emerges only after optimization (constraint violation during optimization is B.3). Do not apply if the solver simply produces too few or too many circles (B.5). Do not apply to refiner or checker roles.

codes.name: Solver_Incorrect_Constraint_Formulation
codes.description: Solver constructs incorrect geometric constraints — wrong boundary conditions, incorrect pairwise overlap expressions, off-by-one indexing in the constraint loop, or missing constraint terms — such that the optimization problem is mis-specified. The observable consequence is that the solver produces a configuration containing geometric constraint violations (overlaps between circles, boundary violations, or negative radii) even though the optimization nominally converged. Covers both the root cause (malformed constraints) and the output symptom (violated geometry in the produced solution).
codes.when_to_use: Apply when the solver's output configuration contains measurable geometric violations (circle-circle overlaps, circles extending outside the container boundary, negative radii) attributable to how the solver expressed or enforced its constraints, including cases where the optimization reports success but the solution is geometrically invalid. Also apply when code inspection reveals constraint expressions that are algebraically incorrect, use wrong indices, or omit required terms.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not apply when violations are introduced by the refiner after the solver produced a valid solution (use B.13). Do not apply when the checker incorrectly reports a violating solution as valid (use B.6). Do not apply when the circle count is wrong rather than the geometry being violated (use B.5). Do not apply to degenerate initial placement specifically (use B.1 as the more precise code if the failure is strictly at initialization).

codes.name: Solver_Wrong_Circle_Count
codes.description: Solver generates a configuration with fewer or more than the required N=26 circles, either by truncating the placement loop, over-generating and failing to trim, or using a hardcoded count that differs from the problem specification.
codes.when_to_use: When the output circle list length does not equal the required N. Apply regardless of whether the geometric constraints on the present circles are satisfied.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not apply when the count is correct but circles are geometrically invalid (use B.3). Do not apply to checker or refiner roles.

codes.name: Checker_False_Validation_Pass
codes.description: Checker reports no violations (empty boundary_violations, overlaps, negative_radii lists) for a solution that actually contains constraint violations, due to incorrect tolerance thresholds, wrong distance formulae, missing iteration over all pairs, or logic errors in the validation code.
codes.when_to_use: When an independent geometric audit of a solution that the checker passed reveals actual violations. Apply when the checker's validation logic is traceable as the source of the missed detection.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not apply when the checker correctly identifies violations. Do not apply when the checker crashes or produces no output (system failure, not a quality-of-work issue). Do not apply when the solver produced a valid solution that the checker correctly passed.

codes.name: Coordinator_Stale_Best_Solution_Propagation
codes.description: Coordinator passes an outdated, incorrect, or lower-quality current_best_solution reference to the next iteration — either from a failed run (score=0), a previous iteration that has since been superseded, or by failing to update the best-solution register after a successful improvement. The failure occurs at the handoff and selection stage, which is the coordinator's responsibility.
codes.when_to_use: When the coordinator's output message or state shows it is forwarding a solution whose score is lower than a solution already produced in a prior iteration, or when the coordinator forwards a solution from a failed/invalid run. The failure must be locatable in the coordinator's selection or propagation logic, not in the refiner's subsequent processing.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not apply when the refiner itself discards or overwrites the correctly-passed best solution (use B.12). Do not apply when there is no prior valid solution to propagate (first iteration). Do not apply to solver or checker roles.

codes.name: Refiner_Prior_Solution_Discarded
codes.description: Refiner receives a high-quality current_best_solution but produces a worse output by overwriting the best-known configuration with a newly generated or re-optimized configuration that scores lower, rather than using the prior solution as the incumbent and only replacing it upon genuine improvement. The failure occurs during the refinement computation itself, which is the refiner's responsibility.
codes.when_to_use: When the refiner's output solution has a lower sum_of_radii (or more violations) than the current_best_solution it received as input, indicating it did not treat the input as a floor to beat. Apply when the coordinator correctly passed a valid high-quality solution and the regression is traceable to the refiner's internal logic.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not apply when the coordinator passed a stale or low-quality solution (the regression originates upstream — use B.9). Do not apply when the refiner intentionally restarts from scratch per the coordinator's instruction. Do not apply to solver or checker roles.

codes.name: Refiner_Constraint_Relaxation_During_Refinement
codes.description: Refiner applies an optimization that improves the objective (sum of radii) by inadvertently relaxing geometric constraints — allowing slight boundary violations or circle overlaps — rather than achieving a genuine feasible improvement. The output appears better by the objective metric but is geometrically invalid.
codes.when_to_use: When the refiner's output shows a higher sum_of_radii than the input best solution but also contains constraint violations not present in the input, indicating the gain was obtained by relaxing rather than satisfying constraints.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not apply when the refiner produces a genuinely feasible improvement (higher score, no new violations). Do not apply when constraint violations were already present in the input solution passed to the refiner (violations originated upstream). Do not apply to solver or checker roles.

codes.name: Negative_Radius_From_Unconstrained_Joint_Optimization
codes.description: When radii are included as optimization variables alongside centers in a joint formulation, the optimizer produces negative radii because the lower bound constraint r_i >= 0 is missing, ill-formed, or violated by the optimizer.
codes.when_to_use: When the output circles array contains negative radius values and the code uses a joint optimizer over (x, y, r) variables where radii are directly optimized rather than computed from centers via LP.
codes.when_not_to_use: When radii are computed from centers via LP (always non-negative by construction). Do not apply when negative values appear from numerical noise at exactly r=0 (e.g., -1e-10) in an otherwise valid LP solution.

codes.name: Degenerate_Circle_With_Near_Zero_Radius
codes.description: One or more circles in the final solution are assigned a radius at or near the minimum floor value (e.g., 1e-6 or 0.001), contributing negligibly to the objective. This indicates a center placement in a region with no available space, which a correct algorithm would either avoid or reassign.
codes.when_to_use: When validation details show min_radius near 1e-6 or a similarly tiny floor value, and inspection of the circle array confirms one or more entries with r ≈ 0, indicating wasted degrees of freedom in the packing.
codes.when_not_to_use: When all radii are meaningfully positive (e.g., min_radius > 0.05). Do not apply solely because a circle is smaller than others — only when the radius is effectively zero (at or near the enforced minimum floor).

codes.name: Penalty_Method_Constraint_Softening
codes.description: Hard geometric constraints (non-overlap, boundary containment) are replaced by soft penalty terms added to the objective function. This allows the optimizer to explore infeasible regions and may converge to a solution that violates constraints, since the penalty weight may be insufficient to enforce strict feasibility.
codes.when_to_use: When the trace shows an objective function containing penalty terms like 'penalty += pen_weight * overlap**2' or 'penalty += pen_weight * boundary_viol**2' substituting for hard constraints, and either validation reports violations or the achieved score is far below optimal.
codes.when_not_to_use: When penalties are used only to guide the optimizer and the final solution is projected onto the feasible set (e.g., via a separate LP-based radius computation that enforces hard constraints). Do not apply if the penalty is zero at the final solution.

codes.name: Incorrect_Computational_Geometry_Primitive
codes.description: A fundamental computational geometry operation — such as point-in-polygon testing, convex hull construction, Voronoi diagram computation, distance calculation between geometric objects, or circle-circle intersection testing — is implemented with an incorrect algorithm or formula. The error is in the geometric reasoning itself (e.g., using bounding-box containment as a proxy for circle containment, computing chord length instead of center distance, or misidentifying Voronoi cell boundaries), not merely in numerical precision or constraint formulation.
codes.when_to_use: Use when the trace implements a geometric subroutine whose output is provably incorrect for the given inputs based on established computational geometry definitions — e.g., a distance function that returns the wrong value for known test cases, a containment test that accepts points outside the region, or a Voronoi construction that produces cells inconsistent with the input sites.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use for constraint formulation errors in optimization solvers (use C.5), for errors that are purely numerical/floating-point rather than algorithmic, or for cases where the geometry primitive is correct but misapplied to the wrong problem component.

codes.name: Objective_Score_Metric_Confusion
codes.description: The optimization objective is formulated to maximize or minimize a proxy metric (e.g., total area, minimum radius, packing density) instead of the correct metric (sum of radii), causing the optimizer to pursue a different goal than required.
codes.when_to_use: When the objective function or score computation uses area (pi*r^2), minimum radius, average radius, or another quantity in place of the plain sum of radii. Applies when the reasoning explicitly states or codes an incorrect objective.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the code correctly maximizes sum of radii, even if intermediate helper metrics are used. Do not apply when area is used only as a diagnostic printout rather than as the optimization target.

codes.name: SA_Cooling_Schedule_Mismatch
codes.description: The simulated annealing cooling schedule is misconfigured relative to the available time budget, either cooling so fast that the search freezes before exploring the space, or so slowly that temperature never drops enough to converge to a good solution within the time limit.
codes.when_to_use: When SA is used and the cooling rate or number of steps is set without reference to the actual timeout value, or when the schedule is hardcoded with constants that result in either premature freezing (T near zero after a few hundred steps) or near-constant temperature throughout the run.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the SA schedule is explicitly calibrated to the timeout parameter (e.g., 'n_steps = int(timeout * steps_per_second)'). Do not apply when poor scores result from initialization quality rather than the cooling schedule itself.

codes.name: Non_Overlap_Constraint_Formulation_Error
codes.description: The pairwise non-overlap constraint is formulated incorrectly in the LP or gradient optimizer, such as using squared distances instead of Euclidean distances, using strict inequality where non-strict is needed, or indexing pairs incorrectly, causing constraint violations or overly conservative packing.
codes.when_to_use: When the constraint matrix or penalty function for non-overlap uses dist^2 instead of dist, or when pair indexing causes some pairs to be omitted or double-counted, detectable from the mathematical expression in the code.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the constraint is correctly written as r_i + r_j <= euclidean_dist(i, j). Do not apply when greedy radius shrinking is used (use C.1 instead); this code targets algebraically incorrect constraint expressions.

codes.name: Boundary_Constraint_Off_By_One_Or_Missing_Wall
codes.description: The boundary constraint ensuring each circle fits inside the unit square is missing one or more walls (e.g., only checking x >= r but not x + r <= 1), or uses an incorrect margin (e.g., center clipped to [0, 1] instead of [r, 1-r]).
codes.when_to_use: When the boundary check for a circle center omits one of the four wall distances (left, right, top, bottom), or when center clipping uses hard constants like 0.01/0.99 that do not depend on the actual radius, causing boundary violations in the output.
codes.when_not_to_use: When boundary violations appear in validation output but the constraint is correctly formulated (i.e., violations arose from optimizer ignoring correctly stated constraints). Do not apply if all four walls are checked and radii are correctly bounded.

codes.name: Greedy_Radius_Shrinking_Instead_Of_LP
codes.description: Maximum radii are computed by iteratively shrinking overlapping circle pairs rather than solving the exact linear program that maximizes sum of radii subject to non-overlap and boundary constraints. This yields provably suboptimal radii even for a fixed set of centers.
codes.when_to_use: When the trace shows a radius-computation function using loops over pairs, checking overlap, and proportionally scaling down both radii — instead of calling linprog (or equivalent LP solver) with pairwise-distance constraints as upper bounds.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the trace shows linprog being called with a constraint matrix encoding r_i + r_j <= dist(i,j) for all pairs. Do not apply if the iterative approach is used only as a fallback after LP failure.

codes.name: LP_Constraint_Matrix_Rebuilt_Inside_Objective
codes.description: The full O(n²) LP constraint matrix (encoding all pairwise non-overlap constraints) is constructed from scratch inside a function that is called repeatedly by an iterative optimizer. This makes each optimizer iteration O(n²) in setup cost, causing severe slowdown or timeout for n≈26.
codes.when_to_use: When the trace shows A_ub (or equivalent LP matrix) being allocated and filled inside a function that is itself the objective or called inside minimize(), scipy.optimize, or any optimization loop that runs thousands of iterations.
codes.when_not_to_use: When the LP matrix is built once outside the optimization loop, or when it is built inside a function called only a small fixed number of times (e.g., a final post-processing step).

codes.name: Structured_Initialization_Ignoring_Boundary_Effects
codes.description: Circle centers are placed according to a regular geometric pattern (e.g., concentric rings, uniform grid, hexagonal lattice) without adapting spacing, offsets, or ring radii to ensure all initial centers satisfy the boundary constraint. Circles on the outer ring or grid border are placed at or beyond the unit square boundary, causing the initial configuration to be infeasible and requiring immediate clipping or repair that distorts the intended structure.
codes.when_to_use: Use when the trace initializes centers using any regular geometric pattern (ring, grid, lattice) and the resulting initial positions include circles whose centers are outside [r_min, 1-r_min] in either coordinate, or whose center coordinates equal 0 or 1 without radius adjustment.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the initialization pattern explicitly accounts for boundary margins (e.g., grid spacing computed as 1/(k+1) to leave boundary gaps, or ring radii capped at 1/2 - r), or when centers are placed by random sampling within the feasible region.

codes.name: Insufficient_Search_Diversity_And_Warm_Start_Neglect
codes.description: The optimization converges to a suboptimal local optimum due to insufficient exploration of the solution space. This manifests in two related ways: (1) running from only one or a very small number of starting configurations without restarts or global search diversity, and/or (2) a previously computed best solution is available (e.g., loaded from a file or prior run) but is never used as a starting point, causing the optimizer to begin from an arbitrary or random configuration that is worse than what is already known. Both failure modes result in the optimizer lacking the starting-point quality or diversity needed to escape local optima.
codes.when_to_use: Use when the trace shows the optimizer running from a single cold start with no restarts, or when a warm-start solution is explicitly read or referenced in the code but is not passed to or used by the optimizer as an initial point. Applies to any optimization method (gradient descent, SA, LP, etc.).
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use when multiple restarts are attempted with diverse initializations, or when no warm-start solution is available to the run. Do not use when a single initialization is deliberately chosen because the problem is small enough that a single run reliably finds the global optimum.
